meta.what: Atoms: irreducible entries. defined = has a symbol in ATOMS.md; attribute-list only = in the attribute index with no symbol or recipe; implicit = named inside recipes and defined nowhere (added so every ingredient resolves).
meta.key: DOMAIN|Name. Always read the domain with the name; the same name can mean different things in different domains.

ACOUSTIC|Amplitude.name: Amplitude
ACOUSTIC|Amplitude.definition: The magnitude of the pressure wave. Volume/loudness.

ACOUSTIC|Beat.name: Beat
ACOUSTIC|Beat.definition: The periodic amplitude modulation when two close frequencies interfere (pulsing rhythm).

ACOUSTIC|Damping.name: Damping
ACOUSTIC|Damping.definition: The dissipation of sound energy (absorption, friction, scattering).

ACOUSTIC|Echo.name: Echo
ACOUSTIC|Echo.definition: The reflection of a sound wave off a surface. Delay indicates distance.
ACOUSTIC|Echo.condition: Reflected sound arrives after direct sound.

ACOUSTIC|Frequency.name: Frequency
ACOUSTIC|Frequency.definition: The number of oscillations per second (Hz). Pitch: high = treble, low = bass.

ACOUSTIC|Interference.name: Interference
ACOUSTIC|Interference.definition: The superposition of two or more sound waves. Constructive (louder) or destructive (quieter).

ACOUSTIC|Medium.name: Medium
ACOUSTIC|Medium.definition: The substance through which sound travels (gas, liquid, solid). Determines speed.
ACOUSTIC|Medium.condition: Sound speed is finite; depends on medium.

ACOUSTIC|Resonance.name: Resonance
ACOUSTIC|Resonance.definition: The natural frequency of an object. When driven at this frequency, amplitude amplifies dramatically.
ACOUSTIC|Resonance.condition: Amplitude peaks when driving frequency matches natural frequency.

ACOUSTIC|Sound Wave.name: Sound Wave
ACOUSTIC|Sound Wave.definition: A longitudinal mechanical wave propagating through a medium (air, water, solid).

ACOUSTIC|Timbre.name: Timbre
ACOUSTIC|Timbre.definition: The "color" or quality of sound that distinguishes a piano from a violin, even at the same pitch.

ACTION|Agency.name: Agency
ACTION|Agency.definition: The felt sense of "I caused this."

ACTION|Consequence.name: Consequence
ACTION|Consequence.definition: The outcome or effect of the action.

ACTION|Duration.name: Duration
ACTION|Duration.definition: The length of the action. The "how long" of the act.

ACTION|Exertion.name: Exertion
ACTION|Exertion.definition: The energy applied in the act. The "force" or "work" done.
ACTION|Exertion.condition: Work done; force applied over distance.

ACTION|Initiation.name: Initiation
ACTION|Initiation.definition: The moment a choice is made to act. The "spark" of the deed.

ACTION|Meta-Action.name: Meta-Action
ACTION|Meta-Action.definition: An action that modifies other actions. The "act of programming."

ACTION|Precision.name: Precision
ACTION|Precision.definition: The accuracy of the action. Fine motor control.

ACTION|Scope.name: Scope
ACTION|Scope.definition: The range or coverage of the action.

ACTION|Timing.name: Timing
ACTION|Timing.definition: The temporal placement of the action. The "when" of the deed.
ACTION|Timing.condition: Action occurs at a specific time.

ACTION|Will.name: Will
ACTION|Will.definition: The volitional drive that powers action. The "I shall do this."
ACTION|Will.condition: Agent reports wanting to act; persists.

ADHERENCE|Allegiance.name: Allegiance
ADHERENCE|Allegiance.definition: The formal commitment to a cause, group, or authority. The oath.
ADHERENCE|Allegiance.condition: Agent acts in support of the group.

ADHERENCE|Commitment.name: Commitment
ADHERENCE|Commitment.definition: The act of binding oneself to a course of action, person, or principle. The "I shall."
ADHERENCE|Commitment.condition: Agent acts consistently with stated intention.

ADHERENCE|Consistency.name: Consistency
ADHERENCE|Consistency.definition: The adherence to a pattern of behavior or belief across time.

ADHERENCE|Covenant.name: Covenant
ADHERENCE|Covenant.definition: A sacred or binding agreement between parties. A sealed promise.
ADHERENCE|Covenant.condition: Agreement is treated as sacred and unbreakable.

ADHERENCE|Discipline.name: Discipline
ADHERENCE|Discipline.definition: The sustained adherence to a practice, regimen, or set of rules.

ADHERENCE|Fidelity.name: Fidelity
ADHERENCE|Fidelity.definition: Faithfulness to a person, promise, or principle. The quality of being true.

ADHERENCE|Loyalty.name: Loyalty
ADHERENCE|Loyalty.definition: The sustained adherence to a person, group, or cause, often despite difficulty.

ADHERENCE|Promise.name: Promise
ADHERENCE|Promise.definition: A stated commitment that creates an expectation in another. The social bond.

ADHERENCE|Stubbornness.name: Stubbornness
ADHERENCE|Stubbornness.definition: Rigid, inflexible adherence that resists change, even when change is warranted.
ADHERENCE|Stubbornness.condition: Agent does not change despite pressure.

ADHERENCE|Tenacity.name: Tenacity
ADHERENCE|Tenacity.definition: The quality of holding fast. The refusal to let go.
ADHERENCE|Tenacity.condition: Agent maintains grip/position despite opposing forces.

ADVERSARIAL|Contingency.name: Contingency
ADVERSARIAL|Contingency.definition: reciprocal, responsive behaviour signals an agent

ADVERSARIAL|Efficiency.name: Efficiency
ADVERSARIAL|Efficiency.definition: agents take the most efficient available means

ADVERSARIAL|False belief.name: False belief
ADVERSARIAL|False belief.definition: an agent can act on a world-state that is not the case

ADVERSARIAL|Goal attribution.name: Goal attribution
ADVERSARIAL|Goal attribution.definition: actions are directed at a target

ADVERSARIAL|Input model.name: Input model
ADVERSARIAL|Input model.definition: an agent's policy reads a specific function of state

ADVERSARIAL|Level-1 perspective.name: Level-1 perspective
ADVERSARIAL|Level-1 perspective.definition: another agent sees some of the world and not the rest

ADVERSARIAL|Level-2 perspective.name: Level-2 perspective
ADVERSARIAL|Level-2 perspective.definition: another agent sees the same thing differently from where it stands

ADVERSARIAL|Misrepresentation.name: Misrepresentation
ADVERSARIAL|Misrepresentation.definition: act to make another's model wrong

ADVERSARIAL|Teleological stance.name: Teleological stance
ADVERSARIAL|Teleological stance.definition: read action through goal and constraint, without mental states

AESTHETIC|Balance.name: Balance
AESTHETIC|Balance.definition: visual weight distributed across a composition
AESTHETIC|Balance.condition: Moments of visual weight sum to zero about center.

AESTHETIC|Clarity.name: Clarity
AESTHETIC|Clarity.definition: how easily the structure can be read
AESTHETIC|Clarity.condition: Figure‑ground separation is unambiguous; low noise.

AESTHETIC|Contrast.name: Contrast
AESTHETIC|Contrast.definition: difference in brightness, colour, size or shape

AESTHETIC|Gestalt.name: Gestalt
AESTHETIC|Gestalt.definition: the whole exceeding the parts — also Human Gs
AESTHETIC|Gestalt.condition: Group is perceived as a single entity, not sum of parts.

AESTHETIC|Proportion.name: Proportion
AESTHETIC|Proportion.definition: the relationship between the sizes of parts

AESTHETIC|Rhythm.name: Rhythm
AESTHETIC|Rhythm.definition: repetition with variation; a pulse that creates expectation

AESTHETIC|Scale.name: Scale
AESTHETIC|Scale.definition: extent, including extent beyond easy grasp
AESTHETIC|Scale.condition: Object is very large or very small relative to frame.

AESTHETIC|Symmetry.name: Symmetry
AESTHETIC|Symmetry.definition: unchanged under reflection, rotation or translation — also Human Ge
AESTHETIC|Symmetry.condition: Applying transform yields same shape (within tolerance).

AESTHETIC|Unity.name: Unity
AESTHETIC|Unity.definition: the sense that the parts belong together
AESTHETIC|Unity.condition: Parts share common features; perceived as a whole.

ALEATORY|Distribution.name: Distribution
ALEATORY|Distribution.definition: The mathematical function that describes the probabilities of different outcomes (Gaussian, Uniform, Poisson, etc.).
ALEATORY|Distribution.condition: Mathematical function fits the observed frequencies.

ALEATORY|Entropy (stochastic).name: Entropy (stochastic)
ALEATORY|Entropy (stochastic).definition: A measure of uncertainty in a probability distribution. Maximal when all outcomes are equally likely.
ALEATORY|Entropy (stochastic).condition: Entropy = –Σ p log p; maximal when uniform.

ALEATORY|Expectation.name: Expectation
ALEATORY|Expectation.definition: The average outcome of a random process over many repetitions. The "long run."

ALEATORY|Karma.name: Karma
ALEATORY|Karma.definition: The moralized version of luck: the belief that actions (good or bad) generate corresponding consequences, often over multiple lifetimes.
ALEATORY|Karma.condition: Positive actions followed by positive outcomes (and vice versa), often delayed.

ALEATORY|Luck.name: Luck
ALEATORY|Luck.definition: The subjective attribution of positive or negative outcomes to chance, rather than skill.
ALEATORY|Luck.condition: Agent attributes outcome to external chance, not ability.

ALEATORY|Odds.name: Odds
ALEATORY|Odds.definition: The ratio of the probability of an event occurring to the probability of it not occurring.

ALEATORY|Probability.name: Probability
ALEATORY|Probability.definition: A numerical measure of the likelihood of an event (0 to 1). The language of uncertainty.

ALEATORY|Randomness.name: Randomness
ALEATORY|Randomness.definition: The absence of pattern or predictability. True stochasticity.
ALEATORY|Randomness.condition: Sequence passes randomness tests (e.g., no significant autocorrelation).

ALEATORY|Risk.name: Risk
ALEATORY|Risk.definition: The exposure to the possibility of loss or gain. Probability × Consequence.

ATMOSPHERIC|Air Mass.name: Air Mass
ATMOSPHERIC|Air Mass.definition: A large body of gas with uniform temperature, humidity, and pressure. The "chunk" of atmosphere.
ATMOSPHERIC|Air Mass.condition: Over a region, these are homogeneous.

ATMOSPHERIC|Climate.name: Climate
ATMOSPHERIC|Climate.definition: The long-term average of weather patterns in a region. The statistical baseline.

ATMOSPHERIC|Coriolis Effect.name: Coriolis Effect
ATMOSPHERIC|Coriolis Effect.definition: The apparent deflection of moving air due to Earth's rotation. Curves winds.
ATMOSPHERIC|Coriolis Effect.condition: Deflection is to right in Northern Hemisphere.

ATMOSPHERIC|Front.name: Front
ATMOSPHERIC|Front.definition: The boundary between two air masses. Where weather happens.
ATMOSPHERIC|Front.condition: Sharp change in T/H across line.

ATMOSPHERIC|Humidity.name: Humidity
ATMOSPHERIC|Humidity.definition: The amount of water vapor in the air. The invisible fuel for storms.

ATMOSPHERIC|Pressure.name: Pressure
ATMOSPHERIC|Pressure.definition: The weight of the air above a given point. High = fair; Low = stormy.

ATMOSPHERIC|Storm.name: Storm
ATMOSPHERIC|Storm.definition: A severe atmospheric disturbance. Hurricane, tornado, blizzard, thunderstorm.

ATMOSPHERIC|Temperature.name: Temperature
ATMOSPHERIC|Temperature.definition: The average kinetic energy of air molecules. Drives convection and pressure gradients.

ATMOSPHERIC|Visibility.name: Visibility
ATMOSPHERIC|Visibility.definition: The clarity of the air. Fog, haze, rain, or snow reduce visibility.
ATMOSPHERIC|Visibility.condition: Distance to horizon is reduced by fog/haze.

ATMOSPHERIC|Wind.name: Wind
ATMOSPHERIC|Wind.definition: The horizontal movement of air from high to low pressure. The atmosphere's circulation.

AUTOMATON|Automaton.name: Automaton
AUTOMATON|Automaton.definition: A self-operating machine or system. The "one that moves itself."

AUTOMATON|Input.name: Input
AUTOMATON|Input.definition: The data or signal that triggers a transition. The "stimulus."

AUTOMATON|Loop (Automaton).name: Loop (Automaton)
AUTOMATON|Loop (Automaton).definition: A repeated cycle of transitions. The "iteration."

AUTOMATON|Output.name: Output
AUTOMATON|Output.definition: The result of a transition. The "response."

AUTOMATON|Process.name: Process
AUTOMATON|Process.definition: An automated sequence of actions. The "running program."

AUTOMATON|Program.name: Program
AUTOMATON|Program.definition: A set of rules that defines a sequence of operations. The "code."
AUTOMATON|Program.condition: The assembly of rules into a program; the "coding of the automaton."

AUTOMATON|Transition.name: Transition
AUTOMATON|Transition.definition: The change from one state to another. The "step."

CELLULAR|Bacteriophage.name: Bacteriophage
CELLULAR|Bacteriophage.definition: A virus that infects bacteria. The "predator" of the microbial world.

CELLULAR|Biofilm.name: Biofilm
CELLULAR|Biofilm.definition: A structured community of bacteria embedded in a self-produced matrix. The "city" of microbes.

CELLULAR|Cell.name: Cell
CELLULAR|Cell.definition: The fundamental unit of life. A membrane-bound, self-replicating entity containing genetic material and metabolic machinery.
CELLULAR|Cell.condition: Has membrane, DNA, ribosomes; can divide.

CELLULAR|DNA.name: DNA
CELLULAR|DNA.definition: The genetic blueprint of the cell. The instructions for building and replicating.

CELLULAR|Eukaryote.name: Eukaryote
CELLULAR|Eukaryote.definition: A complex cell with a nucleus and organelles (plants, animals, fungi). The "building block" of multicellular life.

CELLULAR|Membrane.name: Membrane
CELLULAR|Membrane.definition: The boundary of the cell. The selective barrier that defines inside and outside.

CELLULAR|Metabolism (Cellular).name: Metabolism (Cellular)
CELLULAR|Metabolism (Cellular).definition: The network of chemical reactions that provide energy and building blocks.

CELLULAR|Prokaryote.name: Prokaryote
CELLULAR|Prokaryote.definition: A simple, ancient cell without a nucleus (bacteria, archaea). The "original" life.

CELLULAR|Quorum Sensing.name: Quorum Sensing
CELLULAR|Quorum Sensing.definition: Bacterial communication via chemical signals. The "language" of colonies.

CELLULAR|Ribosome.name: Ribosome
CELLULAR|Ribosome.definition: The protein-building machinery of the cell. The "translator" of genetic code.

CHARACTER|Agency (Character).name: Agency (Character)
CHARACTER|Agency (Character).definition: Acting according to character despite pressure
CHARACTER|Agency (Character).condition: Agent resists pressure and acts on values.

CHARACTER|Authenticity.name: Authenticity
CHARACTER|Authenticity.definition: The degree to which one's actions align with one's true self.

CHARACTER|Conscience.name: Conscience
CHARACTER|Conscience.definition: The internal voice that judges one's actions against one's moral framework.
CHARACTER|Conscience.condition: Agent experiences guilt and corrects wrongdoing.

CHARACTER|Identity.name: Identity
CHARACTER|Identity.definition: The persistent sense of self across time. The "who" that endures.

CHARACTER|Integrity.name: Integrity
CHARACTER|Integrity.definition: The coherence between one's beliefs, words, and actions. Walking the talk.

CHARACTER|Moral Framework.name: Moral Framework
CHARACTER|Moral Framework.definition: The internal system of values and principles that guides judgment.
CHARACTER|Moral Framework.condition: Judgments follow a consistent set of principles.

CHARACTER|Narrative Identity.name: Narrative Identity
CHARACTER|Narrative Identity.definition: The internal story one tells about oneself. The self as a story.
CHARACTER|Narrative Identity.condition: Agent has a coherent life story.

CHARACTER|Reputation.name: Reputation
CHARACTER|Reputation.definition: The collective perception of one's character by others. The social mirror.
CHARACTER|Reputation.condition: Others have a consistent view of the agent.

CHARACTER|Vice.name: Vice
CHARACTER|Vice.definition: A stable, negative disposition to act against a value (cowardice, deceit, cruelty).
CHARACTER|Vice.condition: Agent reliably acts against a positive value.

CHARACTER|Virtue.name: Virtue
CHARACTER|Virtue.definition: A stable, positive disposition to act in accordance with a value (courage, honesty, compassion).
CHARACTER|Virtue.condition: Agent reliably acts in accordance with a positive value.

CHEMICAL|Acidity.name: Acidity
CHEMICAL|Acidity.definition: where a thing sits between sour and soapy

CHEMICAL|Activation energy.name: Activation energy
CHEMICAL|Activation energy.definition: the minimum needed to start it at all
CHEMICAL|Activation energy.condition: Reaction only occurs above a certain temperature.

CHEMICAL|Bond.name: Bond
CHEMICAL|Bond.condition: Atoms are at equilibrium distance; bond energy is negative (stable).

CHEMICAL|Catalyst.name: Catalyst
CHEMICAL|Catalyst.definition: speeds a change without being used up
CHEMICAL|Catalyst.condition: Reaction rate increases but catalyst amount unchanged.

CHEMICAL|Compound.name: Compound
CHEMICAL|Compound.definition: two or more bound into a unit

CHEMICAL|Electron transfer.name: Electron transfer
CHEMICAL|Electron transfer.condition: Oxidation state of one species increases, another decreases.

CHEMICAL|Element.name: Element
CHEMICAL|Element.condition: Substance consists of only one type of atom.

CHEMICAL|Equilibrium.name: Equilibrium
CHEMICAL|Equilibrium.definition: forward and reverse happening at the same rate

CHEMICAL|Ratio.name: Ratio
CHEMICAL|Ratio.definition: the fixed proportion reactants combine in

CHOICE|Alternative.name: Alternative
CHOICE|Alternative.definition: A possible option or pathway. A branch point in the decision space.
CHOICE|Alternative.condition: At least two distinct options available.

CHOICE|Commitment.name: Commitment
CHOICE|Commitment.definition: The binding of the will to a selected alternative. The point of no return.
CHOICE|Commitment.condition: Choice is made; cannot be easily undone.

CHOICE|Constraint.name: Constraint
CHOICE|Constraint.definition: A factor that limits or shapes the set of available alternatives.

CHOICE|Decision Basis.name: Decision Basis
CHOICE|Decision Basis.definition: The information and criteria used to select among alternatives.
CHOICE|Decision Basis.condition: Choices are based on available information.

CHOICE|Decision Latency.name: Decision Latency
CHOICE|Decision Latency.definition: The time taken to make a choice. Hesitation vs. impulsivity.

CHOICE|Flexibility.name: Flexibility
CHOICE|Flexibility.definition: The ability to change a choice after commitment.
CHOICE|Flexibility.condition: Choice can be altered after initial commitment.

CHOICE|Meta-Choice.name: Meta-Choice
CHOICE|Meta-Choice.definition: A choice about how to make choices.

CHOICE|Preference.name: Preference
CHOICE|Preference.definition: The subjective ranking of alternatives. The "what I want" of the system.
CHOICE|Preference.condition: Agent consistently chooses one over another.

CHOICE|Regret.name: Regret
CHOICE|Regret.definition: The negative emotion associated with a chosen outcome vs. a rejected alternative.
CHOICE|Regret.condition: Agent reports wishing they had chosen differently.

CHOICE|Risk.name: Risk
CHOICE|Risk.definition: The uncertainty associated with the outcome of an alternative.

CONNECTION|Affinity.name: Affinity
CONNECTION|Affinity.definition: The natural attraction or compatibility between entities. The "pull."

CONNECTION|Edge.name: Edge
CONNECTION|Edge.definition: The connection between nodes in a network. The "line."

CONNECTION|Entanglement.name: Entanglement
CONNECTION|Entanglement.definition: A deep, non-local correlation that persists across distance. The "quantum bond."

CONNECTION|Interdependence.name: Interdependence
CONNECTION|Interdependence.definition: The mutual reliance of entities on each other. The "we belong."
CONNECTION|Interdependence.condition: Entities depend on each other for survival.

CONNECTION|Link.name: Link
CONNECTION|Link.definition: A direct connection between two entities. The "thread."

CONNECTION|Network.name: Network
CONNECTION|Network.definition: A structure of interconnected nodes and edges. The "web."

CONNECTION|Nexus.name: Nexus
CONNECTION|Nexus.definition: A central point of connection where many links converge. The "hub."

CONNECTION|Relationship.name: Relationship
CONNECTION|Relationship.definition: The dynamic interaction between two or more entities. The "between."
CONNECTION|Relationship.condition: Entities affect each other over time.

CONNECTION|Resonance.name: Resonance
CONNECTION|Resonance.definition: The sympathetic vibration that synchronizes connected systems. The "tuning."

CONNECTION|Wholeness.name: Wholeness
CONNECTION|Wholeness.definition: The emergent property of a connected system. The "greater than the sum."

CURIOSITY|Awe.name: Awe
CURIOSITY|Awe.definition: The emotional response to vastness that exceeds one's current understanding.

CURIOSITY|Discovery.name: Discovery
CURIOSITY|Discovery.definition: The moment of finding something new, previously unknown.

CURIOSITY|Epistemic Curiosity.name: Epistemic Curiosity
CURIOSITY|Epistemic Curiosity.definition: The desire for knowledge, understanding, and the filling of information gaps.
CURIOSITY|Epistemic Curiosity.condition: Agent seeks information to fill gap.

CURIOSITY|Exploration.name: Exploration
CURIOSITY|Exploration.definition: The active, behavioral seeking of new information and experiences.

CURIOSITY|Information Gap.name: Information Gap
CURIOSITY|Information Gap.definition: The cognitive tension between what is known and what is unknown.
CURIOSITY|Information Gap.condition: Agent reports “I don’t know” and wants to know.

CURIOSITY|Inquisitiveness.name: Inquisitiveness
CURIOSITY|Inquisitiveness.definition: The stable disposition to ask questions and seek answers.

CURIOSITY|Novelty.name: Novelty
CURIOSITY|Novelty.definition: The attraction to the new, the unfamiliar, the unexpected.

CURIOSITY|Question.name: Question
CURIOSITY|Question.definition: The cognitive act of inquiry. The "what, why, how" of the mind.

CURIOSITY|Surprise.name: Surprise
CURIOSITY|Surprise.definition: The emotional response to a violation of expectation. The fuel of curiosity.

CURIOSITY|Wonder.name: Wonder
CURIOSITY|Wonder.definition: The emotional response to the mysterious, vast, or awe-inspiring. The "wow" of the unknown.

CYBERNETIC|Damping.name: Damping
CYBERNETIC|Damping.definition: The reduction of oscillation over time. Friction for control.

CYBERNETIC|Error Signal.name: Error Signal
CYBERNETIC|Error Signal.definition: The difference between the current state and the desired state (setpoint). The driver of correction.

CYBERNETIC|Feedback.name: Feedback
CYBERNETIC|Feedback.definition: The return of output to input. The circular flow of information.

CYBERNETIC|Gain.name: Gain
CYBERNETIC|Gain.definition: The amplification factor of the feedback loop. Too high = instability; Too low = sluggishness.

CYBERNETIC|Homeostasis.name: Homeostasis
CYBERNETIC|Homeostasis.definition: The active maintenance of a stable internal environment via negative feedback.
CYBERNETIC|Homeostasis.condition: Variable stays within narrow range despite perturbation.

CYBERNETIC|Negative Feedback.name: Negative Feedback
CYBERNETIC|Negative Feedback.definition: A loop that reduces the error. Stabilizing. Homeostasis.

CYBERNETIC|Oscillation.name: Oscillation
CYBERNETIC|Oscillation.definition: Cyclic behavior caused by feedback that is too slow or gain that is too high.

CYBERNETIC|Positive Feedback.name: Positive Feedback
CYBERNETIC|Positive Feedback.definition: A loop that amplifies the error. Destabilizing. Runaway.

CYBERNETIC|Servomechanism.name: Servomechanism
CYBERNETIC|Servomechanism.definition: An automatic device that uses feedback to correct its performance.
CYBERNETIC|Servomechanism.condition: Output tracks reference with minimal error.

CYBERNETIC|Setpoint.name: Setpoint
CYBERNETIC|Setpoint.definition: The target state that the system is trying to achieve. The "goal."
CYBERNETIC|Setpoint.condition: System attempts to maintain variable at this value.

DESIRE|Aspiration.name: Aspiration
DESIRE|Aspiration.definition: A long-term, often ideal, desire that orients a life. The "I hope to become."

DESIRE|Craving.name: Craving
DESIRE|Craving.definition: An intense, often urgent, desire that can override other concerns. The "I must have now."

DESIRE|Drive.name: Drive
DESIRE|Drive.definition: The internal motivational force that propels action toward a goal.

DESIRE|Frustration.name: Frustration
DESIRE|Frustration.definition: The negative feeling that arises when desire is blocked. The "I cannot have."

DESIRE|Goal.name: Goal
DESIRE|Goal.definition: A cognitive representation of a desired future state. The "toward which."
DESIRE|Goal.condition: Agent acts to achieve a specific state.

DESIRE|Liking.name: Liking
DESIRE|Liking.definition: The hedonic component of desire. The "pleasure" rather than the "pull."

DESIRE|Need.name: Need
DESIRE|Need.definition: A requirement for survival, flourishing, or psychological well-being. The "I must."

DESIRE|Satisfaction.name: Satisfaction
DESIRE|Satisfaction.definition: The positive feeling that arises when desire is fulfilled. The "I have."

DESIRE|Want.name: Want
DESIRE|Want.definition: The felt inclination toward a specific object, state, or outcome. The "I would like."

DESIRE|Wanting (vs. Liking).name: Wanting (vs. Liking)
DESIRE|Wanting (vs. Liking).definition: The motivational component of desire. The "pull" rather than the "pleasure."

DYNAMIC|Coupling.name: Coupling
DYNAMIC|Coupling.definition: how strongly parts interact; high syncs, low is independent
DYNAMIC|Coupling.condition: High correlation or mutual information between parts.

DYNAMIC|Damping.name: Damping
DYNAMIC|Damping.condition: Oscillations decay over time; damping ratio > 0.

DYNAMIC|Latency.name: Latency
DYNAMIC|Latency.definition: delay between a stimulus and its response

DYNAMIC|Recovery.name: Recovery
DYNAMIC|Recovery.definition: how fast resource returns after a demand
DYNAMIC|Recovery.condition: Resource increases over time when not in use.

DYNAMIC|Resource.name: Resource
DYNAMIC|Resource.definition: consumable fuel that depletes with activity
DYNAMIC|Resource.condition: Resource decreases over time as activity occurs.

DYNAMIC|Response.name: Response
DYNAMIC|Response.definition: what the system does about it
DYNAMIC|Response.condition: System produces an output or change after stimulus.

DYNAMIC|Sensitivity.name: Sensitivity
DYNAMIC|Sensitivity.definition: how much a small input amplifies

DYNAMIC|Stimulus.name: Stimulus
DYNAMIC|Stimulus.definition: input arriving; energy put into the system
DYNAMIC|Stimulus.condition: A change in external variable > threshold is detected.

DYNAMIC|Threshold.name: Threshold
DYNAMIC|Threshold.definition: the point at which behaviour changes abruptly
DYNAMIC|Threshold.condition: Output changes sharply at a specific input value.

DYNAMIC|Variance.name: Variance
DYNAMIC|Variance.definition: how much it fluctuates — also Raw data T1

ECONOMIC|Cost.name: Cost
ECONOMIC|Cost.definition: what is given up to get it, including what else you could have done
ECONOMIC|Cost.condition: The agent sacrifices measurable resources or alternatives.

ECONOMIC|Game.name: Game
ECONOMIC|Game.definition: interaction where your payoff depends on others' choices
ECONOMIC|Game.condition: Payoff of one player depends on choice of at least one other.

ECONOMIC|Incentive.name: Incentive
ECONOMIC|Incentive.definition: a reward or penalty that shapes behaviour

ECONOMIC|Information asymmetry.name: Information asymmetry
ECONOMIC|Information asymmetry.definition: one side knows more than the other
ECONOMIC|Information asymmetry.condition: One agent has private information not available to others.

ECONOMIC|Resource.name: Resource
ECONOMIC|Resource.definition: anything that can be spent or exchanged
ECONOMIC|Resource.condition: Object has a measurable quantity and can be used/traded.

ECONOMIC|Risk.name: Risk
ECONOMIC|Risk.condition: Multiple possible outcomes with known probabilities.

ECONOMIC|Scarcity.name: Scarcity
ECONOMIC|Scarcity.condition: Demand > supply at zero price; price > 0.

ECONOMIC|Trade.name: Trade
ECONOMIC|Trade.definition: voluntary exchange; both sides prefer what they receive
ECONOMIC|Trade.condition: Both parties’ utility increases after exchange.

ECONOMIC|Utility.name: Utility
ECONOMIC|Utility.condition: Agent chooses bundle that ranks highest in their preference order.

ECONOMIC|Value.name: Value
ECONOMIC|Value.definition: what a thing is worth to a particular agent
ECONOMIC|Value.condition: Agent trades something of known value to acquire it.

ELECTRICAL|Magnetic field.name: Magnetic field
ELECTRICAL|Magnetic field.definition: a field made by moving charge

EMBODIMENT|Agency.name: Agency
EMBODIMENT|Agency.definition: The subjective feeling of "I caused this action," distinct from the action itself.
EMBODIMENT|Agency.condition: Perceived time between action and outcome is compressed; self‑report.

EMBODIMENT|Body Schema.name: Body Schema
EMBODIMENT|Body Schema.definition: The dynamic, plastic neural representation of the body's structure and boundaries.
EMBODIMENT|Body Schema.condition: Touch on a body part is localised to that part in space.

EMBODIMENT|Boundary.name: Boundary
EMBODIMENT|Boundary.definition: The felt distinction between "me" (my body) and "not-me" (the external world).
EMBODIMENT|Boundary.condition: Body parts are perceived as own; external objects are not.

EMBODIMENT|Efference copy.name: Efference copy
EMBODIMENT|Efference copy.definition: A predictive signal sent alongside motor commands; predicts the sensory consequence of self-action.
EMBODIMENT|Efference copy.condition: predictedSensation matches actualSensation when action is self‑caused.

EMBODIMENT|Haptics.name: Haptics
EMBODIMENT|Haptics.definition: Sense of touch, pressure, texture, and vibration through the skin and muscles.
EMBODIMENT|Haptics.condition: Tactile receptors signal presence and properties of contact.

EMBODIMENT|Interoception.name: Interoception
EMBODIMENT|Interoception.definition: Sense of the internal state of the body (heartbeat, breathing, hunger, fatigue, pain).
EMBODIMENT|Interoception.condition: Signals from internal organs are detectable and accurate.

EMBODIMENT|Kinesthesia.name: Kinesthesia
EMBODIMENT|Kinesthesia.definition: Sense of movement and force. The "feel" of effort, weight, and resistance.
EMBODIMENT|Kinesthesia.condition: Signals correlate with actual limb movement and force.

EMBODIMENT|Presence.name: Presence
EMBODIMENT|Presence.definition: The subjective feeling of "being inside" the body and located in a specific place.
EMBODIMENT|Presence.condition: Agent reports being located in body; flinch to body‑directed threat.

EMBODIMENT|Proprioception.name: Proprioception
EMBODIMENT|Proprioception.definition: Sense of limb position, angle, and tension. The "sixth sense" of the body in space.
EMBODIMENT|Proprioception.condition: Joint angle reported matches actual angle.

EMBODIMENT|Vestibular.name: Vestibular
EMBODIMENT|Vestibular.definition: Sense of balance, head tilt, acceleration
EMBODIMENT|Vestibular.condition: Vestibular signals correlate with actual motion.

EMOTION|Affect.name: Affect
EMOTION|Affect.definition: The immediate, embodied physiological response (heart rate, skin conductance, facial expression).

EMOTION|Anger.name: Anger
EMOTION|Anger.definition: A negative, high-arousal state. Signals goal-blockage or injustice. Promotes attack and barrier removal.
EMOTION|Anger.condition: Goal blocked; increased force; high arousal.

EMOTION|Arousal.name: Arousal
EMOTION|Arousal.definition: The intensity of activation: calm ↔ excited; drowsy ↔ alert. The "high/low" axis.
EMOTION|Arousal.condition: High arousal → high heart rate, sweat.

EMOTION|Disgust.name: Disgust
EMOTION|Disgust.definition: A negative, moderate-arousal state. Signals contamination/poison. Promotes rejection and expulsion.

EMOTION|Fear.name: Fear
EMOTION|Fear.definition: A negative, high-arousal state. Signals threat. Promotes avoidance, freezing, or flight.

EMOTION|Joy.name: Joy
EMOTION|Joy.definition: A positive, variable-arousal state. Signals safety/reward. Promotes approach and exploration.

EMOTION|Mood.name: Mood
EMOTION|Mood.definition: A low-intensity, persistent background feeling. Diffuse and long-lasting.

EMOTION|Sadness.name: Sadness
EMOTION|Sadness.definition: A negative, low-arousal state. Signals loss. Promotes withdrawal, reflection, and resource conservation.

EMOTION|Surprise.name: Surprise
EMOTION|Surprise.definition: A neutral, high-arousal state. Signals novelty. Promotes orienting and updating of expectations.

EMOTION|Valence.name: Valence
EMOTION|Valence.definition: The intrinsic attractiveness (positive) or aversiveness (negative) of an experience. The "good/bad" axis.

EXCHANGE|Acceptance.name: Acceptance
EXCHANGE|Acceptance.definition: The agreement to an offer. The "I take this."

EXCHANGE|Agent.name: Agent
EXCHANGE|Agent.definition: An entity capable of initiating exchange. The "who" of the transaction.

EXCHANGE|Consideration.name: Consideration
EXCHANGE|Consideration.definition: The thing of value given in return. The "I give you that."

EXCHANGE|Debt.name: Debt
EXCHANGE|Debt.definition: An obligation to provide future value. The "I owe you."

EXCHANGE|Medium of Exchange.name: Medium of Exchange
EXCHANGE|Medium of Exchange.definition: A standardized resource used to facilitate exchange (money, tokens).

EXCHANGE|Offer.name: Offer
EXCHANGE|Offer.definition: A proposal to engage in an exchange. The "I give you this."

EXCHANGE|Reciprocity.name: Reciprocity
EXCHANGE|Reciprocity.definition: The mutual exchange of value. The "give and take."

EXCHANGE|Resource.name: Resource
EXCHANGE|Resource.definition: A good, service, or value that is exchanged. The "what" of the transaction.

EXCHANGE|Value.name: Value
EXCHANGE|Value.definition: The worth or utility attributed to a resource. The "why" of the transaction.
EXCHANGE|Value.condition: Agent gives up something to obtain it.

FLUID|Buoyancy.name: Buoyancy
FLUID|Buoyancy.definition: a submerged thing is pushed up
FLUID|Buoyancy.condition: Upward force = weight of displaced fluid (Archimedes); object feels lighter.

FLUID|Flowing substance.name: Flowing substance
FLUID|Flowing substance.definition: a continuous thing that runs downhill

FLUID|Laminar flow.name: Laminar flow
FLUID|Laminar flow.condition: Streamlines are parallel and non‑crossing; velocity profiles are smooth and predictable.

FLUID|Pressure.name: Pressure
FLUID|Pressure.definition: force spread over an area — also Heat T1

FLUID|Surface tension.name: Surface tension
FLUID|Surface tension.condition: At the fluid edge, there is a measurable surface energy; droplets form spheres; pressure difference across curved surface.

FLUID|Viscosity.name: Viscosity
FLUID|Viscosity.condition: Viscosity = shear stress / strain rate; measured value > 0.

HABIT|Automaticity.name: Automaticity
HABIT|Automaticity.definition: The transfer of an action from conscious to unconscious control.
HABIT|Automaticity.condition: Action performed with low attention; high speed; resistant to interference.

HABIT|Contextual Trigger.name: Contextual Trigger
HABIT|Contextual Trigger.definition: The specific environment or state that activates a habit.

HABIT|Cue / Trigger.name: Cue / Trigger
HABIT|Cue / Trigger.definition: The stimulus that initiates a habitual action. The "if" of the loop.

HABIT|Frequency.name: Frequency
HABIT|Frequency.definition: The rate of repetition. The "how often" of the habit.

HABIT|Inertia.name: Inertia
HABIT|Inertia.definition: The tendency of a system to continue its current behavior.
HABIT|Inertia.condition: The tendency to continue an action simply because it has been started.

HABIT|Novelty.name: Novelty
HABIT|Novelty.definition: The capacity to break or override a habit in response to new information.
HABIT|Novelty.condition: Novel stimulus causes habit to stop.

HABIT|Reward.name: Reward
HABIT|Reward.definition: The positive outcome that reinforces the loop. The "because" of the loop.
HABIT|Reward.condition: Outcome is positive and increases future likelihood.

HABIT|Routine.name: Routine
HABIT|Routine.condition: Actions are performed in fixed order.

HABIT|Strength.name: Strength
HABIT|Strength.definition: The resistance of a habit to disruption. The "stickiness."

HEAT|Conductivity.name: Conductivity
HEAT|Conductivity.definition: how fast heat crosses a material — Electrical T1 has the charge version

HEAT|Heat.name: Heat
HEAT|Heat.definition: energy moving from hot to cold

HEAT|Latent heat.name: Latent heat
HEAT|Latent heat.definition: energy absorbed or released at a phase change

HEAT|Pressure.name: Pressure
HEAT|Pressure.definition: force spread over an area — also Fluid T1

HEAT|Specific heat.name: Specific heat
HEAT|Specific heat.definition: how much heat a thing needs to warm

HEAT|Volume.name: Volume
HEAT|Volume.definition: how much space a thing takes

HUMAN|Animacy.name: Animacy
HUMAN|Animacy.definition: motion without contact indicates an agent
HUMAN|Animacy.condition: Object changes velocity without any detectable external force (no collision, no gravity‑only).

HUMAN|Causality.name: Causality
HUMAN|Causality.condition: If event A precedes B and changing A changes B, then A causes B (confirmed).

HUMAN|Cohesion.name: Cohesion
HUMAN|Cohesion.definition: objects move as connected, bounded wholes
HUMAN|Cohesion.condition: For all parts, relativeDisplacement(i,j) < threshold and relativeVelocity(i,j) < threshold for the duration of movement.

HUMAN|Continuity.name: Continuity
HUMAN|Continuity.condition: No sudden jumps; distance(prevPos, nextPos) <= maxSpeed * dt for all consecutive frames; no gaps in path.

HUMAN|Forward model.name: Forward model
HUMAN|Forward model.definition: predict the sensory consequence of your own action, subtract it
HUMAN|Forward model.condition: The predictedState matches actualState within a tolerance; predictive error is small.

HUMAN|Geometry.name: Geometry
HUMAN|Geometry.condition: Measures of spatial relations (e.g., angle between two lines) are available and consistent.

HUMAN|Gestalt.name: Gestalt
HUMAN|Gestalt.definition: grouping by proximity, similarity, common fate
HUMAN|Gestalt.condition: Objects with similar features and small distances are grouped; common motion (same velocity) strengthens grouping.

HUMAN|Number.name: Number
HUMAN|Number.definition: exact for small sets, approximate above
HUMAN|Number.condition: For n ≤ 4, count is exact (no error); for larger sets, approximate with known Weber‑Fechner limits.

HUMAN|Solidity.name: Solidity
HUMAN|Solidity.definition: two things cannot occupy one place
HUMAN|Solidity.condition: For any two objects, overlapArea == 0 (or distance(centers) > sumOfRadii) at all times.

HUMAN|Statistics.name: Statistics
HUMAN|Statistics.condition: Probabilities of transitions can be estimated from observed sequences; prediction error is low.

HUMAN|Support.name: Support
HUMAN|Support.definition: an unsupported thing falls; stability depends on contact
HUMAN|Support.condition: If contactPoints is empty, then verticalAcceleration must be positive (downward) and velocity increases downward.

HUMAN|Topology.name: Topology
HUMAN|Topology.condition: Containment relations are well‑defined; e.g., pointA is inside objectB is true/false.

INFORMATION|Compression.name: Compression
INFORMATION|Compression.condition: Compressed size is smaller than original; redundancy is eliminated.

INFORMATION|Digest.name: Digest
INFORMATION|Digest.definition: a one-way map to a fixed size

INFORMATION|Search.name: Search
INFORMATION|Search.definition: finding a target in a space

INFORMATION|Shannon entropy.name: Shannon entropy
INFORMATION|Shannon entropy.definition: how much a message could have said

INFORMATION|Structure.name: Structure
INFORMATION|Structure.definition: how data is arranged: list, tree, graph

KINETIC|Articulation.name: Articulation
KINETIC|Articulation.definition: how many degrees of freedom the body has

KINETIC|Balance.name: Balance
KINETIC|Balance.definition: the centre of mass held over the base
KINETIC|Balance.condition: Projection of COM falls within support polygon.

KINETIC|Contact.name: Contact
KINETIC|Contact.definition: interaction with a surface or a medium — also the Human prior
KINETIC|Contact.condition: Number of contact points > 0; normal force > 0.

KINETIC|Gait.name: Gait
KINETIC|Gait.definition: the rhythmic sequence of limb movements
KINETIC|Gait.condition: Limbs move in a repeating, coordinated pattern; phase offsets are consistent.

KINETIC|Inertia.name: Inertia
KINETIC|Inertia.definition: resistance to a change in velocity
KINETIC|Inertia.condition: a = F/m; larger mass → smaller acceleration for same force.

KINETIC|Lift.name: Lift
KINETIC|Lift.definition: force opposing gravity, aerodynamic or buoyant
KINETIC|Lift.condition: Upward force > 0; if object is flying or floating.

KINETIC|Medium.name: Medium
KINETIC|Medium.definition: what is being traversed — ground, water, air, nothing
KINETIC|Medium.condition: Medium is classified as solid, liquid, gas, or vacuum.

KINETIC|Propulsion.name: Propulsion
KINETIC|Propulsion.definition: force generated to overcome inertia — push, pull, thrust, contract
KINETIC|Propulsion.condition: force = mass × acceleration; force is internal (not from collision).

KINETIC|Traction.name: Traction
KINETIC|Traction.definition: grip between the mover and the medium; high holds, low slides

LARGE-SCALE|Horizon.name: Horizon
LARGE-SCALE|Horizon.definition: a boundary past which nothing returns

LARGE-SCALE|Time dilation.name: Time dilation
LARGE-SCALE|Time dilation.definition: clocks run differently in different conditions

LEARNING|Application.name: Application
LEARNING|Application.definition: The use of knowledge in practice. The "action."

LEARNING|Attention (Learning).name: Attention (Learning)
LEARNING|Attention (Learning).definition: The selective focus on specific information. The "gate."

LEARNING|Expertise.name: Expertise
LEARNING|Expertise.definition: Deep, integrated mastery of a domain. The "mastery."

LEARNING|Processing.name: Processing
LEARNING|Processing.definition: The transformation of raw information into usable knowledge. The "analysis."

LEARNING|Reflection.name: Reflection
LEARNING|Reflection.definition: The consideration of one's own learning process. The "meta."

LEARNING|Sensation.name: Sensation
LEARNING|Sensation.definition: The raw intake of information from the environment. The "input."

LEARNING|Storage (Learning).name: Storage (Learning)
LEARNING|Storage (Learning).definition: The retention of knowledge over time. The "memory."

LEARNING|Transfer (Learning).name: Transfer (Learning)
LEARNING|Transfer (Learning).definition: The application of knowledge from one domain to another. The "generalization."

LINEAGE|Ancestor.name: Ancestor
LINEAGE|Ancestor.definition: The one from whom the lineage descends. The root of the tree.

LINEAGE|Branch.name: Branch
LINEAGE|Branch.definition: A divergent line of descent. The split in the tree.

LINEAGE|Descendant.name: Descendant
LINEAGE|Descendant.definition: The one who continues the lineage. The branch of the tree.

LINEAGE|Dynasty.name: Dynasty
LINEAGE|Dynasty.definition: A powerful, enduring line of descent. The "king's line."

LINEAGE|Fruit.name: Fruit
LINEAGE|Fruit.definition: The harvest of a lineage. The "outcome" of the line.

LINEAGE|Gene (Lineage).name: Gene (Lineage)
LINEAGE|Gene (Lineage).definition: The unit of inheritance. The carrier of essence across generations.
LINEAGE|Gene (Lineage).condition: Segment passed from parent to offspring.

LINEAGE|Inheritance.name: Inheritance
LINEAGE|Inheritance.definition: The transmission of traits, resources, or essence from ancestors to descendants.

LINEAGE|Legacy.name: Legacy
LINEAGE|Legacy.definition: The enduring mark left by a lineage. The "what remains."

LINEAGE|Seed.name: Seed
LINEAGE|Seed.definition: The origin point of a lineage. The potential, the source, the beginning.

LINGUISTIC|Metaphor.name: Metaphor
LINGUISTIC|Metaphor.definition: Understanding one thing in terms of another. The bridge between domains.
LINGUISTIC|Metaphor.condition: One domain is understood in terms of another; a systematic set of correspondences exists.

LINGUISTIC|Morpheme.name: Morpheme
LINGUISTIC|Morpheme.definition: The smallest unit of meaning (word, prefix, suffix). The atomic particle of semantic content.
LINGUISTIC|Morpheme.condition: Component carries meaning; can't be split further.

LINGUISTIC|Narrative.name: Narrative
LINGUISTIC|Narrative.definition: The structuring of events into a causal, meaningful story with beginning, middle, and end.
LINGUISTIC|Narrative.condition: Events are connected causally and temporally.

LINGUISTIC|Phoneme.name: Phoneme
LINGUISTIC|Phoneme.definition: The smallest unit of sound that distinguishes meaning. The atomic particle of spoken language.
LINGUISTIC|Phoneme.condition: Two sounds differ and change meaning (e.g., /p/ vs /b/).

LINGUISTIC|Pragmatics.name: Pragmatics
LINGUISTIC|Pragmatics.definition: The use of language in context. What the speaker *intends* and what the listener *infers*.
LINGUISTIC|Pragmatics.condition: Meaning depends on context and speaker’s intent.

LINGUISTIC|Semantics.name: Semantics
LINGUISTIC|Semantics.definition: The mapping from symbols to meaning. What words and sentences *point to* in the world.
LINGUISTIC|Semantics.condition: Symbol refers to a specific object/event.

LINGUISTIC|Signified.name: Signified
LINGUISTIC|Signified.definition: The mental concept the signifier points to. The meaning.

LINGUISTIC|Signifier.name: Signifier
LINGUISTIC|Signifier.definition: The physical form of the symbol (sound, mark, gesture).

LINGUISTIC|Syntax.name: Syntax
LINGUISTIC|Syntax.definition: The structural rules of combination (grammar). How pieces fit together to form larger structures.
LINGUISTIC|Syntax.condition: Sentences are well‑formed according to grammar.

LINGUISTIC|Text.name: Text
LINGUISTIC|Text.definition: A structured sequence of symbols that conveys meaning. The artifact of language.
LINGUISTIC|Text.condition: Symbols arranged in a coherent, meaningful order.

LIVING|Code.name: Code
LIVING|Code.definition: a sequence that specifies a form

LIVING|Energy store.name: Energy store
LIVING|Energy store.definition: held energy, spent to do work

LIVING|Feedback loop.name: Feedback loop
LIVING|Feedback loop.definition: The information that reinforces or weakens a habit.
LIVING|Feedback loop.condition: Error signal drives a response that reduces the error; variable stays near setpoint.

LOGISTICAL|Bottleneck.name: Bottleneck
LOGISTICAL|Bottleneck.definition: A point of congestion where flow is constrained by limited capacity. The rate-limiting step.
LOGISTICAL|Bottleneck.condition: Arrival rate > service rate; queue builds.

LOGISTICAL|Edge.name: Edge
LOGISTICAL|Edge.definition: A connection between nodes. A road, pipe, conveyor, or link. Has capacity and cost.

LOGISTICAL|Flow.name: Flow
LOGISTICAL|Flow.definition: The movement of resources through a network. Rate of transfer per unit time.
LOGISTICAL|Flow.condition: Rate > 0; resource moves from source to sink.

LOGISTICAL|Inventory.name: Inventory
LOGISTICAL|Inventory.definition: Stored resources waiting to be used or moved. A buffer against uncertainty.
LOGISTICAL|Inventory.condition: Stock level changes as inflow minus outflow; can be positive (buffer) or zero.

LOGISTICAL|Node.name: Node
LOGISTICAL|Node.definition: A point in a network where resources are processed, stored, or transferred. A junction.
LOGISTICAL|Node.condition: Entity has defined location and processes resources.

LOGISTICAL|Queue.name: Queue
LOGISTICAL|Queue.definition: A waiting line. Resources waiting for service. Has length, wait time, and priority.

LOGISTICAL|Schedule.name: Schedule
LOGISTICAL|Schedule.definition: A temporal plan for moving resources through the network. When and in what order.

LOGISTICAL|Supply Chain.name: Supply Chain
LOGISTICAL|Supply Chain.definition: The end-to-end sequence of production, distribution, and consumption of a resource.
LOGISTICAL|Supply Chain.condition: Multiple linked stages from raw material to consumer.

LOGISTICAL|Throughput.name: Throughput
LOGISTICAL|Throughput.definition: The rate at which a system processes resources. Output per unit time.

LOGISTICAL|Waste.name: Waste
LOGISTICAL|Waste.definition: Resources that are lost, unused, or inefficiently allocated (muda).

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Absurd.name: Absurd
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Absurd.definition: That which defies logic, reason, or expectation. The "nonsense."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Comedy.name: Comedy
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Comedy.definition: The structure and performance of humor. The "art of laughter."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Incongruity.name: Incongruity
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Incongruity.definition: The clash or mismatch of two incompatible frameworks. The "I wasn't expecting that."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Incongruity.condition: Expectation is violated in a surprising way.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Irony.name: Irony
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Irony.definition: The gap between appearance and reality, between expression and intention.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Irony.condition: Saying opposite of what is meant.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Joke.name: Joke
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Joke.definition: The specific unit of humor. The "setup and punchline."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Laughter.name: Laughter
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Laughter.definition: The physiological, emotional, and social response to humor. The "release."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Relief.name: Relief
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Relief.definition: The cognitive and emotional release that laughter provides. The "tension broken."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Satire.name: Satire
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Satire.definition: The use of humor to critique, expose, or ridicule.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Slapstick.name: Slapstick
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Slapstick.definition: Physical, often exaggerated, humor. The fall, the pie, the pratfall.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Wit.name: Wit
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Wit.definition: The capacity for quick, intelligent, and playful humor.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Wit.condition: Response is fast and clever; evokes laughter.

LUDOLOGICAL|Constitutive Rule.name: Constitutive Rule
LUDOLOGICAL|Constitutive Rule.definition: The formal, abstract rules that define the game's logic (e.g., chess piece moves). Inviolable.
LUDOLOGICAL|Constitutive Rule.condition: Moves that violate rules are disallowed.

LUDOLOGICAL|Game State.name: Game State
LUDOLOGICAL|Game State.definition: The complete description of the game at a given moment. All positions, scores, resources.
LUDOLOGICAL|Game State.condition: State fully determines future legal moves.

LUDOLOGICAL|Implicit Rule.name: Implicit Rule
LUDOLOGICAL|Implicit Rule.definition: The unspoken social rules of play (e.g., "don't be a sore loser").
LUDOLOGICAL|Implicit Rule.condition: Players enforce unwritten rules (e.g., no excessive taunting).

LUDOLOGICAL|Magic Circle.name: Magic Circle
LUDOLOGICAL|Magic Circle.definition: The boundary between the game and reality. Inside the circle, the game's rules apply.
LUDOLOGICAL|Magic Circle.condition: Inside, game rules apply; outside, real‑world rules apply.

LUDOLOGICAL|Metagame.name: Metagame
LUDOLOGICAL|Metagame.definition: The game *about* the game. Strategy selection, counter-strategies, tier lists.
LUDOLOGICAL|Metagame.condition: Players choose strategies based on others’ strategy choices.

LUDOLOGICAL|Objective.name: Objective
LUDOLOGICAL|Objective.definition: The goal of the game. The state that constitutes "winning."
LUDOLOGICAL|Objective.condition: Game ends when a specified state is reached.

LUDOLOGICAL|Operational Rule.name: Operational Rule
LUDOLOGICAL|Operational Rule.definition: The rules that players actually follow (the "how to play" instructions).
LUDOLOGICAL|Operational Rule.condition: Players act according to written/known rules.

LUDOLOGICAL|Score.name: Score
LUDOLOGICAL|Score.definition: A quantitative measure of performance. Not necessarily the same as winning.
LUDOLOGICAL|Score.condition: Score changes according to actions; can be compared.

LUDOLOGICAL|Termination.name: Termination
LUDOLOGICAL|Termination.condition: Game stops when win/loss/draw conditions met.

LUDOLOGICAL|Turn.name: Turn
LUDOLOGICAL|Turn.definition: The discrete unit of play; a player's opportunity to act.
LUDOLOGICAL|Turn.condition: Players act one at a time in fixed order.

MATERIAL|Creep.name: Creep
MATERIAL|Creep.definition: Time-dependent, slow, permanent deformation under constant stress (like a glacier flowing).
MATERIAL|Creep.condition: Strain increases over time at constant stress.

MATERIAL|Elasticity.name: Elasticity
MATERIAL|Elasticity.definition: Ability to deform under stress and *fully recover* when stress is removed. Linear region (Hooke's Law).
MATERIAL|Elasticity.condition: For stress < yield, strain is reversible.

MATERIAL|Fatigue.name: Fatigue
MATERIAL|Fatigue.definition: Progressive weakening under cyclic loading (repeated stress). Cumulative damage over time.
MATERIAL|Fatigue.condition: Failure occurs after N cycles at stress below yield.

MATERIAL|Fracture Toughness.name: Fracture Toughness
MATERIAL|Fracture Toughness.definition: Resistance to crack propagation. High = tough (rubber). Low = brittle (glass).
MATERIAL|Fracture Toughness.condition: Material withstands high stress intensity before cracking.

MATERIAL|Hardness.name: Hardness
MATERIAL|Hardness.definition: Resistance to localized surface indentation or scratching.

MATERIAL|Plasticity.name: Plasticity
MATERIAL|Plasticity.definition: Ability to *permanently* deform when stress exceeds the elastic limit. No recovery.

MATERIAL|Strain.name: Strain
MATERIAL|Strain.definition: The deformation of a material relative to its original size (stretch, compress, twist). The "response."

MATERIAL|Stress.name: Stress
MATERIAL|Stress.definition: Force per unit area applied to a material (pressure). The "load" on the system.

MATERIAL|Ultimate Tensile Strength.name: Ultimate Tensile Strength
MATERIAL|Ultimate Tensile Strength.definition: The maximum stress a material can withstand before it begins to neck/rupture. The peak.

MATERIAL|Yield Strength.name: Yield Strength
MATERIAL|Yield Strength.definition: The stress at which a material begins to deform plastically (the threshold of permanent damage).
MATERIAL|Yield Strength.condition: Point where curve deviates from linearity.

MECHANICAL|Fulcrum.name: Fulcrum
MECHANICAL|Fulcrum.definition: the fixed point a lever turns about
MECHANICAL|Fulcrum.condition: The pivot point is stationary while the bar rotates around it.

MECHANICAL|Gear.name: Gear
MECHANICAL|Gear.definition: a toothed wheel passing rotation on
MECHANICAL|Gear.condition: Rotation of one gear causes the other to rotate; ratio = teeth₂/teeth₁; contact is maintained.

MECHANICAL|Lever.name: Lever
MECHANICAL|Lever.definition: a rigid bar turning about a point
MECHANICAL|Lever.condition: A rigid bar pivots about a fixed point; torques balance: F₁ × d₁ = F₂ × d₂.

MECHANICAL|Pulley.name: Pulley
MECHANICAL|Pulley.definition: a wheel that redirects a pull
MECHANICAL|Pulley.condition: A wheel rotates; rope passes over it; tension is the same on both sides (for ideal pulley).

MECHANICAL|Ramp.name: Ramp
MECHANICAL|Ramp.definition: a slope that trades distance for effort
MECHANICAL|Ramp.condition: Effort force needed is reduced by factor sin(θ); load moves up slope.

MECHANICAL|Rope.name: Rope
MECHANICAL|Rope.definition: a flexible link that pulls and does not push

MECHANICAL|Screw.name: Screw
MECHANICAL|Screw.definition: a ramp wrapped round a cylinder
MECHANICAL|Screw.condition: One rotation produces linear displacement equal to the pitch; pitch = distance per turn.

MECHANICAL|Wedge.name: Wedge
MECHANICAL|Wedge.definition: a shape that turns pushing into spreading
MECHANICAL|Wedge.condition: Input force along one direction produces output forces perpendicular to the wedge faces.

MEDICAL|Acute.name: Acute
MEDICAL|Acute.definition: A sudden, intense condition (rapid crisis, infection, trauma).

MEDICAL|Chronic.name: Chronic
MEDICAL|Chronic.definition: A long-lasting, persistent condition (slow decay, autoimmune, degenerative).

MEDICAL|Contagion.name: Contagion
MEDICAL|Contagion.definition: The transmission of a disease from one organism to another.
MEDICAL|Contagion.condition: New case appears after contact with infected case.

MEDICAL|Healing.name: Healing
MEDICAL|Healing.definition: The process of repairing damage and restoring function over time.

MEDICAL|Immunity.name: Immunity
MEDICAL|Immunity.definition: The system's ability to recognize and neutralize pathogens/toxins.

MEDICAL|Infection.name: Infection
MEDICAL|Infection.definition: The establishment of a pathogen within a host, causing damage.
MEDICAL|Infection.condition: A pathogen breaches the host's defences and begins to replicate; damage accumulates.

MEDICAL|Inflammation.name: Inflammation
MEDICAL|Inflammation.definition: The local response to injury or infection. Heat, redness, swelling, pain.
MEDICAL|Inflammation.condition: Signs present at site of injury.

MEDICAL|Pathogen.name: Pathogen
MEDICAL|Pathogen.definition: A biological agent that causes disease (virus, bacteria, fungus, prion).

MEDICAL|Toxin.name: Toxin
MEDICAL|Toxin.definition: A poisonous substance that disrupts biological function (chemical, biological, radiological).

MEDICAL|Wound.name: Wound
MEDICAL|Wound.definition: A structural breach or trauma that disrupts function (cut, burn, fracture).

MNEMONIC|Decay.name: Decay
MNEMONIC|Decay.definition: The gradual weakening of a trace over time (forgetting curve).

MNEMONIC|Encoding.name: Encoding
MNEMONIC|Encoding.definition: The process of transforming experience into a memory trace. Attention and meaning gate encoding.
MNEMONIC|Encoding.condition: Higher attention leads to better recall.

MNEMONIC|Episodic Memory.name: Episodic Memory
MNEMONIC|Episodic Memory.definition: Memory for specific events, with spatiotemporal context (the "what, where, when").

MNEMONIC|Interference.name: Interference
MNEMONIC|Interference.definition: The disruption of retrieval by other traces (proactive/retroactive).
MNEMONIC|Interference.condition: New learning impairs recall of old (retroactive), or vice versa (proactive).

MNEMONIC|Memory Trace.name: Memory Trace
MNEMONIC|Memory Trace.definition: The physical or informational substrate of a memory (engram, synaptic change, data record).
MNEMONIC|Memory Trace.condition: Physical change correlates with learned information.

MNEMONIC|Primacy Effect.name: Primacy Effect
MNEMONIC|Primacy Effect.definition: Better recall for items at the beginning of a list.
MNEMONIC|Primacy Effect.condition: Items early in list recalled more.

MNEMONIC|Recency Effect.name: Recency Effect
MNEMONIC|Recency Effect.definition: Better recall for items at the end of a list.
MNEMONIC|Recency Effect.condition: Items late in list recalled more.

MNEMONIC|Retrieval.name: Retrieval
MNEMONIC|Retrieval.definition: The process of accessing a stored trace. Recall and recognition.
MNEMONIC|Retrieval.condition: Response to cue is accurate; latency correlates with strength.

MNEMONIC|Semantic Memory.name: Semantic Memory
MNEMONIC|Semantic Memory.definition: Memory for general facts and knowledge, independent of context.
MNEMONIC|Semantic Memory.condition: Recall is independent of learning context.

MNEMONIC|Storage.name: Storage
MNEMONIC|Storage.definition: The maintenance of the trace over time. Consolidation stabilizes the trace.

MORPHOGENETIC|Autocatalysis.name: Autocatalysis
MORPHOGENETIC|Autocatalysis.definition: A reaction where the product catalyzes its own production (positive feedback, self-amplification).

MORPHOGENETIC|Buckling.name: Buckling
MORPHOGENETIC|Buckling.definition: Mechanical instability causing a flat sheet to deform into folds or wrinkles.

MORPHOGENETIC|Cell Adhesion.name: Cell Adhesion
MORPHOGENETIC|Cell Adhesion.definition: The tendency of cells to stick together. Differential adhesion drives tissue sorting.
MORPHOGENETIC|Cell Adhesion.condition: Cells maintain contact; separation requires force.

MORPHOGENETIC|Diffusion.name: Diffusion
MORPHOGENETIC|Diffusion.definition: The random, passive spreading of particles (morphogens) from high to low concentration.

MORPHOGENETIC|Gradient.name: Gradient
MORPHOGENETIC|Gradient.definition: A spatial concentration slope that provides positional information (French flag model).

MORPHOGENETIC|Inhibition.name: Inhibition
MORPHOGENETIC|Inhibition.definition: A reaction where one morphogen suppresses the production of another (negative feedback, antagonism).
MORPHOGENETIC|Inhibition.condition: High A lowers production rate of B.

MORPHOGENETIC|Morphogenetic Field.name: Morphogenetic Field
MORPHOGENETIC|Morphogenetic Field.definition: A spatially organized distribution of signals and forces that coordinates development.
MORPHOGENETIC|Morphogenetic Field.condition: Signals/forces have spatial pattern guiding development.

MORPHOGENETIC|Reaction.name: Reaction
MORPHOGENETIC|Reaction.definition: The local chemical transformation of one morphogen into another.
MORPHOGENETIC|Reaction.condition: Concentration of reactant decreases, product increases.

MORPHOGENETIC|Self-Assembly.name: Self-Assembly
MORPHOGENETIC|Self-Assembly.definition: The spontaneous organization of components into a larger, functional structure without external direction.

MORPHOGENETIC|Turing Instability.name: Turing Instability
MORPHOGENETIC|Turing Instability.definition: A reaction-diffusion system where diffusion destabilizes the homogeneous state, creating spontaneous patterns (spots, stripes).

NETWORK|Bridge.name: Bridge
NETWORK|Bridge.definition: An edge that connects two clusters. The "chokepoint."
NETWORK|Bridge.condition: Removing it increases number of components.

NETWORK|Centrality.name: Centrality
NETWORK|Centrality.definition: The measure of a node's importance within a network. The "hub-ness."

NETWORK|Clustering.name: Clustering
NETWORK|Clustering.definition: The tendency of nodes to form tightly connected groups. The "clique."

NETWORK|Degree.name: Degree
NETWORK|Degree.definition: The number of connections a node has. The "popularity."

NETWORK|Edge.name: Edge
NETWORK|Edge.definition: A link between two nodes. The "connection."

NETWORK|Flow (Network).name: Flow (Network)
NETWORK|Flow (Network).definition: The movement of resources, information, or energy through the network. The "current."

NETWORK|Hub.name: Hub
NETWORK|Hub.condition: Degree is much higher than average.

NETWORK|Node.name: Node
NETWORK|Node.definition: A point of connection in a network. The "vertex."

NETWORK|Topology (Network).name: Topology (Network)
NETWORK|Topology (Network).definition: The shape or structure of a network. The "architecture."

NOETIC|Awakening.name: Awakening
NOETIC|Awakening.definition: A permanent shift in perspective from ego-centered to awareness-centered.
NOETIC|Awakening.condition: Lasting change in perspective; not transient.

NOETIC|Awe.name: Awe
NOETIC|Awe.definition: The feeling of vastness and wonder that transcends ordinary experience.

NOETIC|Dissolution.name: Dissolution
NOETIC|Dissolution.definition: The temporary or permanent loss of the ego boundary. Self and world merge.

NOETIC|Ego.name: Ego
NOETIC|Ego.definition: The sense of a separate, bounded self. The "I" that experiences and acts.
NOETIC|Ego.condition: Agent distinguishes “I” from others; has bodily ownership.

NOETIC|Flow State.name: Flow State
NOETIC|Flow State.definition: Optimal experience. Total immersion, loss of self-consciousness, time distortion, intrinsic reward.
NOETIC|Flow State.condition: Agent reports total immersion; time flies; performance high.

NOETIC|Grace.name: Grace
NOETIC|Grace.definition: An unearned, spontaneous gift of understanding or transformation.

NOETIC|Insight.name: Insight
NOETIC|Insight.definition: A sudden, non-linear, deep understanding that reconfigures perception.

NOETIC|Mindfulness.name: Mindfulness
NOETIC|Mindfulness.definition: The disciplined cultivation of non-judgmental attention to the present moment.

NOETIC|Silence.name: Silence
NOETIC|Silence.definition: The absence of mental chatter. The quieting of the inner monologue.

NOETIC|Union.name: Union
NOETIC|Union.definition: The felt sense of oneness with the universe, others, or the divine.
NOETIC|Union.condition: Reports merging of self and external.

NUTRITIONAL|Absorption.name: Absorption
NUTRITIONAL|Absorption.definition: The passage of broken-down nutrients across a membrane into the internal environment.

NUTRITIONAL|Anabolism.name: Anabolism
NUTRITIONAL|Anabolism.definition: The synthesis of complex molecules from simpler ones (endothermic).

NUTRITIONAL|Catabolism.name: Catabolism
NUTRITIONAL|Catabolism.definition: The breakdown of complex molecules to release energy (exothermic).

NUTRITIONAL|Digestion.name: Digestion
NUTRITIONAL|Digestion.definition: The mechanical and chemical breakdown of substrates into absorbable components.
NUTRITIONAL|Digestion.condition: Large molecules broken into smaller ones.

NUTRITIONAL|Energy Balance.name: Energy Balance
NUTRITIONAL|Energy Balance.definition: The relationship between energy intake and energy expenditure (Input - Output).

NUTRITIONAL|Energy Currency.name: Energy Currency
NUTRITIONAL|Energy Currency.definition: The molecular unit of energy transfer. The fuel that powers work.

NUTRITIONAL|Excretion.name: Excretion
NUTRITIONAL|Excretion.definition: The removal of metabolic waste products. The residue of energy use.

NUTRITIONAL|Ingestion.name: Ingestion
NUTRITIONAL|Ingestion.definition: The intake of substrates into the system. The act of eating.

NUTRITIONAL|Metabolism.name: Metabolism
NUTRITIONAL|Metabolism.definition: The sum of all chemical reactions that convert nutrients into energy and biomass.

NUTRITIONAL|Substrate/Food.name: Substrate/Food
NUTRITIONAL|Substrate/Food.definition: The raw material from which energy and building blocks are extracted.

ONTOLOGICAL|Axiom.name: Axiom
ONTOLOGICAL|Axiom.definition: A self-evident truth that cannot be derived from other truths. The foundation.
ONTOLOGICAL|Axiom.condition: Accepted without proof; used to derive others.

ONTOLOGICAL|Existence.name: Existence
ONTOLOGICAL|Existence.definition: The brute fact of "is." The state of being real, present, or actual.
ONTOLOGICAL|Existence.condition: Object can be observed or detected.

ONTOLOGICAL|Frame.name: Frame
ONTOLOGICAL|Frame.definition: The context that defines what is "inside" and "outside." The boundary of the game.
ONTOLOGICAL|Frame.condition: Entities inside follow different rules than outside.

ONTOLOGICAL|Illusion.name: Illusion
ONTOLOGICAL|Illusion.definition: An appearance that does not match reality. A veil, a deception, a dream.

ONTOLOGICAL|Reality.name: Reality
ONTOLOGICAL|Reality.definition: The totality of all that exists. The sum total of what is the case.

ONTOLOGICAL|Self.name: Self
ONTOLOGICAL|Self.definition: The persistent sense of "I" that experiences reality. The experiencer.

ONTOLOGICAL|Simulation.name: Simulation
ONTOLOGICAL|Simulation.definition: A reality that is generated by an underlying algorithm or process.
ONTOLOGICAL|Simulation.condition: Discrete nature, rendering glitches, finite resolution.

ONTOLOGICAL|Void.name: Void
ONTOLOGICAL|Void.definition: The absence of existence. The nothing from which being emerges.

OPTICAL|Absorption.name: Absorption
OPTICAL|Absorption.definition: Light is absorbed by a material, turning into heat (Thermo).

OPTICAL|Diffraction.name: Diffraction
OPTICAL|Diffraction.definition: Light spreads as it passes through an aperture or around an edge.
OPTICAL|Diffraction.condition: Interference pattern with central maximum and sidelobes.

OPTICAL|Dispersion.name: Dispersion
OPTICAL|Dispersion.definition: The splitting of white light into its constituent colors (chromatic separation, n(λ)).

OPTICAL|Interference.name: Interference
OPTICAL|Interference.definition: Two or more light waves superpose; constructive (bright) or destructive (dark) patterns.
OPTICAL|Interference.condition: Intensity varies with path difference; bright/dark fringes.

OPTICAL|Light Ray.name: Light Ray
OPTICAL|Light Ray.definition: A straight-line path of light propagation. The fundamental "arrow" of optics.
OPTICAL|Light Ray.condition: Light travels in a straight line until reflected/refracted.

OPTICAL|Polarization.name: Polarization
OPTICAL|Polarization.definition: The orientation of the electric field of a light wave (linear, circular).
OPTICAL|Polarization.condition: Intensity varies with polarizer angle (Malus’ law).

OPTICAL|Reflection.name: Reflection
OPTICAL|Reflection.definition: Light bounces off a surface. Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
OPTICAL|Reflection.condition: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.

OPTICAL|Refraction.name: Refraction
OPTICAL|Refraction.definition: Light bends as it passes between mediums (Snell's Law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂).
OPTICAL|Refraction.condition: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

PATHOLOGICAL|Catharsis.name: Catharsis
PATHOLOGICAL|Catharsis.definition: The emotional release and purification that comes through suffering. The "cleansing."

PATHOLOGICAL|Despair.name: Despair
PATHOLOGICAL|Despair.definition: The total loss of hope. The "no way out."

PATHOLOGICAL|Endurance.name: Endurance
PATHOLOGICAL|Endurance.definition: The capacity to persist through unbearable pain. The "holding on."

PATHOLOGICAL|Grief.name: Grief
PATHOLOGICAL|Grief.definition: The deep, slow, enduring response to loss. The "mourning."

PATHOLOGICAL|Mortality.name: Mortality
PATHOLOGICAL|Mortality.definition: The awareness of inevitable death. The "final countdown."

PATHOLOGICAL|Scar.name: Scar
PATHOLOGICAL|Scar.definition: The permanent mark left by a wound. The "reminder."

PATHOLOGICAL|Transformation.name: Transformation
PATHOLOGICAL|Transformation.definition: The fundamental change wrought by suffering. The "becoming new."
PATHOLOGICAL|Transformation.condition: Person is fundamentally different after suffering.

PATHOLOGICAL|Trauma.name: Trauma
PATHOLOGICAL|Trauma.definition: A wound — physical, emotional, or psychological — that exceeds the system's capacity to integrate. The "fracture."

PATHOLOGICAL|Witness (Pathological).name: Witness (Pathological)
PATHOLOGICAL|Witness (Pathological).definition: The one who sees and acknowledges suffering. The "holder."

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Horizon.name: Horizon
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Horizon.definition: The unthematized background of experience. The fringe of awareness.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Horizon.condition: Peripheral objects are present but not attended.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Intentionality.name: Intentionality
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Intentionality.definition: The directedness of consciousness toward an object. Awareness is always *of* something.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Intentionality.condition: Attention and thought are about something specific.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lifeworld.name: Lifeworld
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lifeworld.definition: The pre-scientific, pre-theoretical world of everyday meaning and experience.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lifeworld.condition: World is taken‑for‑granted; shared with others.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived Body.name: Lived Body
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived Body.definition: The body as experienced from within (subject), not as an object in the world.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived Body.condition: Body is felt as subject, not object.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived Meaning.name: Lived Meaning
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived Meaning.definition: The significance a situation has for the experiencer, prior to interpretation.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived Meaning.condition: A puzzle piece is not just a shape; it is a fragment of a story that invites completion.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Mood.name: Mood
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Mood.definition: The atmospheric, pre-cognitive coloring of experience. The "felt sense" of the world.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Other.name: Other
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Other.definition: The experience of another subject. The Other is not an object; it is a witness.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Other.condition: Other appears as a subject, not object.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Presence.name: Presence
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Presence.definition: The vivid, immediate, here-and-now quality of being-in-the-world.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Presence.condition: Agent feels fully present in the moment.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Temporality.name: Temporality
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Temporality.definition: The internal, pre-reflective flow of time. The lived duration between instants.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Attention.name: Attention
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Attention.definition: selective focus on part of what is available
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Attention.condition: Reaction time faster and accuracy higher for attended stimuli.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Belief.name: Belief
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Belief.definition: an internal model of what is true
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Belief.condition: Agent acts and speaks as if the proposition is true.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Bias.name: Bias
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Bias.definition: systematic departure from what the evidence supports
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Bias.condition: Choices consistently deviate from rational (Bayesian) expectation.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Deliberate control.name: Deliberate control
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Deliberate control.condition: Decisions involve planning; effortful; can override habits.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Habit.name: Habit
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Habit.definition: automatic behaviour triggered by a situation
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Habit.condition: Action occurs automatically upon trigger, with little conscious deliberation.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Heuristic.name: Heuristic
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Heuristic.condition: Decision made quickly using a simple rule, not exhaustive search.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Memory.name: Memory
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Memory.definition: storing and retrieving past states and outcomes
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Memory.condition: Information from past is available later.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Motivation.name: Motivation
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Motivation.definition: drive to close the gap between here and the goal
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Motivation.condition: Persistence increases as distance to goal decreases.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Self-model.name: Self-model
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Self-model.definition: the agent's model of itself as one persisting thing

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Valence.name: Valence
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Valence.definition: positive or negative, calm or aroused; it biases choice
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Valence.condition: Valence is rated positive/negative; arousal high/low.

QUANTUM|Entanglement.name: Entanglement
QUANTUM|Entanglement.definition: two things correlated without a visible link

QUANTUM|Interference.name: Interference
QUANTUM|Interference.condition: The probability at the detector shows constructive/destructive interference; amplitudes add.

QUANTUM|No copying.name: No copying
QUANTUM|No copying.definition: an unknown state cannot be duplicated
QUANTUM|No copying.condition: No unitary operation can produce two independent copies of an arbitrary unknown state; fidelity < 1.

QUANTUM|Superposition.name: Superposition
QUANTUM|Superposition.definition: several candidate states held at once, none chosen

QUANTUM|Tunnelling.name: Tunnelling
QUANTUM|Tunnelling.definition: passing a barrier that should have stopped you

RAW DATA|Entropy.name: Entropy
RAW DATA|Entropy.definition: how unpredictable a distribution is — also Heat, Information, Aleatory

REBELLION|Courage.name: Courage
REBELLION|Courage.definition: The psychological strength to rebel against a powerful system.

REBELLION|Defiance.name: Defiance
REBELLION|Defiance.definition: The active opposition to an authority, rule, or expectation. The "no."

REBELLION|Dissent.name: Dissent
REBELLION|Dissent.definition: The expression of disagreement with a prevailing view or authority.

REBELLION|Heresy.name: Heresy
REBELLION|Heresy.definition: A belief or opinion that diverges from established doctrine or orthodoxy.

REBELLION|Nonconformity.name: Nonconformity
REBELLION|Nonconformity.definition: The refusal to adhere to established norms or conventions.

REBELLION|Principled Disobedience.name: Principled Disobedience
REBELLION|Principled Disobedience.definition: The deliberate violation of a rule on moral or ethical grounds.
REBELLION|Principled Disobedience.condition: Agent violates rule due to moral objection.

REBELLION|Refusal.name: Refusal
REBELLION|Refusal.definition: The conscious choice not to comply with a demand or expectation.

REBELLION|Revolution.name: Revolution
REBELLION|Revolution.definition: The systematic, often collective, overthrow of an existing order.
REBELLION|Revolution.condition: Group acts to replace existing order.

REBELLION|Subversion.name: Subversion
REBELLION|Subversion.definition: The act of undermining or destabilizing a system from within.
REBELLION|Subversion.condition: Agent weakens system while appearing loyal.

REBELLION|Transgression.name: Transgression
REBELLION|Transgression.definition: The act of crossing a boundary or violating a taboo.

SKILL|Adaptability.name: Adaptability
SKILL|Adaptability.definition: The capacity to adjust skill to novel situations. The "flexibility."

SKILL|Economy of Motion.name: Economy of Motion
SKILL|Economy of Motion.definition: The minimization of wasted effort. The "efficiency."

SKILL|Expertise.name: Expertise
SKILL|Expertise.definition: Deep, intuitive mastery of a domain. The "mastery."

SKILL|Flow (Skill).name: Flow (Skill)
SKILL|Flow (Skill).definition: The state of total immersion and effortless performance. The "zone."

SKILL|Fluidity.name: Fluidity
SKILL|Fluidity.definition: The smooth, graceful integration of actions. The "flow."

SKILL|Improvisation.name: Improvisation
SKILL|Improvisation.definition: The creative application of skill in unscripted situations. The "invention."

SKILL|Style.name: Style
SKILL|Style.definition: The distinctive, personal expression of skill. The "signature."

SKILL|Technique.name: Technique
SKILL|Technique.definition: A specific method of performing an action. The "how."
SKILL|Technique.condition: Action can be repeated with same method.

SOCIAL|Culture.name: Culture
SOCIAL|Culture.definition: The shared beliefs, values, norms, and artifacts of a group. Transmitted across generations.
SOCIAL|Culture.condition: Norms and symbols are shared across individuals and generations.

SOCIAL|Group.name: Group
SOCIAL|Group.definition: A collection of individuals who perceive themselves as a collective. Shared identity.

SOCIAL|Herding.name: Herding
SOCIAL|Herding.definition: The tendency of individuals to follow the behavior of others, often without deliberation.
SOCIAL|Herding.condition: Individuals follow the crowd when they are uncertain; an information cascade occurs.

SOCIAL|Individual.name: Individual
SOCIAL|Individual.definition: A single agent with its own goals, beliefs, and preferences. The atomic unit of the social.
SOCIAL|Individual.condition: Entity has persistent identity and distinct goals/beliefs.

SOCIAL|Influence.name: Influence
SOCIAL|Influence.definition: The ability to change the beliefs, preferences, or actions of another agent.
SOCIAL|Influence.condition: After interaction, target’s opinion moves toward source.

SOCIAL|Network.name: Network
SOCIAL|Network.definition: The pattern of connections between individuals (who knows whom, who influences whom).

SOCIAL|Norm.name: Norm
SOCIAL|Norm.definition: An implicit or explicit rule governing behavior within a group. Conformity pressure.
SOCIAL|Norm.condition: Deviations are punished; compliance is rewarded.

SOCIAL|Reputation.name: Reputation
SOCIAL|Reputation.definition: The collective belief about an individual's past behavior. A social signal.

SOCIAL|Role.name: Role
SOCIAL|Role.definition: A set of expected behaviors associated with a position within a group (leader, follower, outcast).
