SOCIAL|Role.condition: Agent performs behaviours associated with that position.

SOCIAL|Trust.name: Trust
SOCIAL|Trust.definition: The expectation that another agent will act in a cooperative manner. Social capital.

SOMNIAL|Circadian Rhythm.name: Circadian Rhythm
SOMNIAL|Circadian Rhythm.definition: The internal, roughly 24-hour biological clock. The rhythm of waking and sleeping.
SOMNIAL|Circadian Rhythm.condition: Regular cycle independent of external cues.

SOMNIAL|Dream.name: Dream
SOMNIAL|Dream.definition: A narrative, symbolic, often surreal sequence of images, sensations, and emotions occurring during sleep.

SOMNIAL|Dream Symbol.name: Dream Symbol
SOMNIAL|Dream Symbol.condition: Dream element is linked to a deeper theme.

SOMNIAL|Hypnagogia.name: Hypnagogia
SOMNIAL|Hypnagogia.definition: The liminal state between waking and sleep. The threshold where imagery flickers and logic softens.

SOMNIAL|NREM Sleep.name: NREM Sleep
SOMNIAL|NREM Sleep.definition: The deeper, restorative stages of sleep (stages 1-3). Slow-wave sleep.

SOMNIAL|Nightmare.name: Nightmare
SOMNIAL|Nightmare.definition: A deeply disturbing, anxiety-provoking dream. The shadow of the night.
SOMNIAL|Nightmare.condition: Dream causes fear; agent wakes distressed.

SOMNIAL|REM Sleep.name: REM Sleep
SOMNIAL|REM Sleep.definition: The stage of sleep characterized by rapid eye movements, vivid dreaming, and near-waking brain activity.

SOMNIAL|Repression.name: Repression
SOMNIAL|Repression.definition: The unconscious blocking of threatening thoughts, impulses, or memories.

SOMNIAL|Restorative.name: Restorative
SOMNIAL|Restorative.definition: The healing, replenishing function of sleep. The "reboot" of the system.

SOMNIAL|Symbol (Dream).name: Symbol (Dream)
SOMNIAL|Symbol (Dream).definition: The dream's language: images that stand for deeper, often hidden meanings.

SOMNIAL|Unconscious.name: Unconscious
SOMNIAL|Unconscious.definition: The vast, submerged part of the psyche; inaccessible to waking consciousness but active in dreams.

TEMPORAL|Anticipation.name: Anticipation
TEMPORAL|Anticipation.definition: The felt sense of a future event. Expectation. Tension before the release.

TEMPORAL|Cooldown.name: Cooldown
TEMPORAL|Cooldown.definition: A mandatory delay after an action before it can be repeated. Recovery time.

TEMPORAL|Countdown.name: Countdown
TEMPORAL|Countdown.definition: A ticking clock. A finite, decreasing resource. The pressure of scarcity.
TEMPORAL|Countdown.condition: A visible or invisible timer; when it reaches zero, an event occurs (good or bad).

TEMPORAL|Duration.name: Duration
TEMPORAL|Duration.definition: The objective length of time an event occupies (seconds, frames). Measurable, uniform.

TEMPORAL|Foresight.name: Foresight
TEMPORAL|Foresight.definition: The cognitive ability to simulate future states. Projecting consequences.
TEMPORAL|Foresight.condition: Predictions about future state are accurate.

TEMPORAL|Lag.name: Lag
TEMPORAL|Lag.definition: A delay between action and consequence. The gap between cause and effect.

TEMPORAL|Retrospection.name: Retrospection
TEMPORAL|Retrospection.definition: The felt sense of a past event. Memory, nostalgia, regret. The weight of what has been.
TEMPORAL|Retrospection.condition: Agent can describe past event; emotional response present.

TEMPORAL|Rhythm.name: Rhythm
TEMPORAL|Rhythm.definition: The pattern of events over time. Regular or irregular intervals. The pulse of the system.
TEMPORAL|Rhythm.condition: Intervals have a repetitive pattern (regular or variable).

TEMPORAL|Synchronization.name: Synchronization
TEMPORAL|Synchronization.definition: The alignment of two or more temporal rhythms. Being "in sync."
TEMPORAL|Synchronization.condition: Phase difference is constant; frequencies are matched.

TEMPORAL|Timing Window.name: Timing Window
TEMPORAL|Timing Window.definition: A specific interval in which an action is valid. Before or after, it fails.

THAUMATURGICAL|Animism/Spirit.name: Animism/Spirit
THAUMATURGICAL|Animism/Spirit.definition: The attribution of agency, will, or soul to inanimate objects or natural forces.
THAUMATURGICAL|Animism/Spirit.condition: Agent describes object as having will or intention.

THAUMATURGICAL|Divination.name: Divination
THAUMATURGICAL|Divination.definition: Perceived pattern in noise for prediction
THAUMATURGICAL|Divination.condition: Agent interprets random event as predictive.

THAUMATURGICAL|Incantation.name: Incantation
THAUMATURGICAL|Incantation.definition: Spoken or written words that are believed to have causal magical power.

THAUMATURGICAL|Magical Link.name: Magical Link
THAUMATURGICAL|Magical Link.definition: A connection between two objects that allows magic to affect one by acting on the other.
THAUMATURGICAL|Magical Link.condition: Agent treats objects as linked despite distance.

THAUMATURGICAL|Ritual.name: Ritual
THAUMATURGICAL|Ritual.definition: A structured sequence of symbolic actions, repeated for a specific magical purpose.
THAUMATURGICAL|Ritual.condition: A fixed sequence of actions is repeated exactly because it worked once; superstitious conditioning.

THAUMATURGICAL|Sympathetic Magic.name: Sympathetic Magic
THAUMATURGICAL|Sympathetic Magic.definition: The principle that like produces like (similarity) and that once connected, always connected (contagion).
THAUMATURGICAL|Sympathetic Magic.condition: Agent treats similar objects as causally linked.

THAUMATURGICAL|Taboo.name: Taboo
THAUMATURGICAL|Taboo.definition: A forbidden action or object. Violating it has magical consequences.
THAUMATURGICAL|Taboo.condition: Violation leads to avoidance or punishment.

THOUGHT|Abstraction.name: Abstraction
THOUGHT|Abstraction.definition: The extraction of essential structure while ignoring surface details.
THOUGHT|Abstraction.condition: Core is retained; details are ignored.

THOUGHT|Analogy.name: Analogy
THOUGHT|Analogy.definition: The mapping of structure from one domain to another. The engine of creativity.

THOUGHT|Concept.name: Concept
THOUGHT|Concept.definition: A mental representation of a category, object, or idea. The building block of thought.
THOUGHT|Concept.condition: Object is assigned to a class.

THOUGHT|Imagination.name: Imagination
THOUGHT|Imagination.definition: The generation of mental simulations, scenarios, and counterfactuals.

THOUGHT|Inference.name: Inference
THOUGHT|Inference.definition: The movement from one proposition to another. The "therefore" of logic.

THOUGHT|Logic.name: Logic
THOUGHT|Logic.definition: The formal rules of valid inference. The "calculus" of thought.

THOUGHT|Meta-Thought.name: Meta-Thought
THOUGHT|Meta-Thought.definition: Thinking about thinking. Reflection on the process of thought itself.

THOUGHT|Proposition.name: Proposition
THOUGHT|Proposition.definition: A mental statement that can be true or false. The unit of belief and reasoning.
THOUGHT|Proposition.condition: Agent acts as if proposition is true/false.

THOUGHT|Rhetoric.name: Rhetoric
THOUGHT|Rhetoric.definition: The art of persuasive thought. The "appeal" dimension of reasoning.

THOUGHT|Syllogism.name: Syllogism
THOUGHT|Syllogism.definition: A formal structure of reasoning (Major premise → Minor premise → Conclusion).
THOUGHT|Syllogism.condition: A formal deductive argument; major premise → minor premise → conclusion.

TOPOLOGICAL|Boundary.name: Boundary
TOPOLOGICAL|Boundary.definition: The edge of a manifold. A surface that separates inside from outside.
TOPOLOGICAL|Boundary.condition: Points that have no open neighbourhood entirely inside.

TOPOLOGICAL|Dimensionality.name: Dimensionality
TOPOLOGICAL|Dimensionality.definition: The number of independent coordinates needed to specify a point (1D, 2D, 3D, 4D...).
TOPOLOGICAL|Dimensionality.condition: Minimum number of coordinates to specify a point.

TOPOLOGICAL|Elliptic Space.name: Elliptic Space
TOPOLOGICAL|Elliptic Space.definition: A space of constant positive curvature (sphere). Parallel lines converge; triangles sum to more than 180°.

TOPOLOGICAL|Fractal Dimension.name: Fractal Dimension
TOPOLOGICAL|Fractal Dimension.definition: A dimension that is not an integer (e.g., 1.5). Self-similarity across scales.

TOPOLOGICAL|Genus.name: Genus
TOPOLOGICAL|Genus.definition: The number of "holes" in a surface (0 = sphere, 1 = torus, 2 = double torus, etc.). A fundamental invariant.

TOPOLOGICAL|Hyperbolic Space.name: Hyperbolic Space
TOPOLOGICAL|Hyperbolic Space.definition: A space of constant negative curvature. Parallel lines diverge; triangles have angles summing to less than 180°.

TOPOLOGICAL|Knot.name: Knot
TOPOLOGICAL|Knot.definition: An embedding of a circle into 3D space that is not unknotted. A tangled loop.

TOPOLOGICAL|Orientability.name: Orientability
TOPOLOGICAL|Orientability.definition: Whether a surface has two distinct sides (orientable) or one (non-orientable, like a Möbius strip).
TOPOLOGICAL|Orientability.condition: Normal vector flips sign after a loop (non‑orientable).

TOPOLOGICAL|Projective Space.name: Projective Space
TOPOLOGICAL|Projective Space.definition: A space where parallel lines meet at infinity. Non-orientable.
TOPOLOGICAL|Projective Space.condition: Lines converge to a point at infinity.

TOPOLOGICAL|Topological Invariant.name: Topological Invariant
TOPOLOGICAL|Topological Invariant.definition: A property that does not change under continuous deformation (homeomorphism). The number of holes (genus), connected components, and boundary components.

TRANSFORMATION|Becoming.name: Becoming
TRANSFORMATION|Becoming.definition: The process of moving from one form to another. The "what it is becoming."

TRANSFORMATION|Catalyst.name: Catalyst
TRANSFORMATION|Catalyst.definition: Agent precipitating change without being consumed

TRANSFORMATION|Emergence.name: Emergence
TRANSFORMATION|Emergence.definition: The arising of new properties from a transformation. The "novelty."

TRANSFORMATION|Form.name: Form
TRANSFORMATION|Form.definition: The current state or shape of a thing. The "what it is."

TRANSFORMATION|Metamorphosis.name: Metamorphosis
TRANSFORMATION|Metamorphosis.definition: A dramatic, complete change of form. The "rebirth."
TRANSFORMATION|Metamorphosis.condition: A complete, dramatic transformation of a being.

TRANSFORMATION|Mutation.name: Mutation
TRANSFORMATION|Mutation.definition: A change in fundamental nature. The "alteration."

TRANSFORMATION|Phase Transition.name: Phase Transition
TRANSFORMATION|Phase Transition.definition: The change of state (solid, liquid, gas, plasma). The "shift."

TRANSFORMATION|Transmutation.name: Transmutation
TRANSFORMATION|Transmutation.definition: The conversion of one substance into another. The "alchemy."

ZOOLOGICAL|Camouflage / Crypsis.name: Camouflage / Crypsis
ZOOLOGICAL|Camouflage / Crypsis.definition: The ability to blend into the environment to avoid detection.

ZOOLOGICAL|Ecological Niche.name: Ecological Niche
ZOOLOGICAL|Ecological Niche.definition: The role and position of an organism in its environment. What it eats, how it moves, when it sleeps.
ZOOLOGICAL|Ecological Niche.condition: Species has specific resource use and habitat.

ZOOLOGICAL|Instinct.name: Instinct
ZOOLOGICAL|Instinct.definition: An innate, fixed pattern of behavior. Hardwired. Triggered by specific stimuli (sign stimuli).
ZOOLOGICAL|Instinct.condition: Behaviour occurs without learning; triggered by specific cue.

ZOOLOGICAL|Migration.name: Migration
ZOOLOGICAL|Migration.definition: Periodic, long-distance movement in response to seasons or resources.
ZOOLOGICAL|Migration.condition: Regular movement over long distances with seasons.

ZOOLOGICAL|Mimicry.name: Mimicry
ZOOLOGICAL|Mimicry.definition: Imitating the appearance or behavior of another species (Batesian, Müllerian).

ZOOLOGICAL|Predation.name: Predation
ZOOLOGICAL|Predation.definition: The hunting and consuming of one organism (prey) by another (predator).
ZOOLOGICAL|Predation.condition: Predator actively catches and eats prey.

ZOOLOGICAL|Prey.name: Prey
ZOOLOGICAL|Prey.definition: An organism that is hunted and consumed. Evolves defenses.

ZOOLOGICAL|Sensory Modality.name: Sensory Modality
ZOOLOGICAL|Sensory Modality.definition: The specific way an animal perceives the world (sight, hearing, smell, vibration, electroreception).

ZOOLOGICAL|Territoriality.name: Territoriality
ZOOLOGICAL|Territoriality.definition: The defense of a specific area against others of the same species.
